record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: What is the minimum exponent of a repetion which is avoidable by an infinite word constructed by iterated (prefix)-suffix duplication?

evidence.quote: What is the minimum exponent of a repetion which is avoidable by an infinite word constructed by iterated (prefix)-suffix duplication?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $w \in \Sigma^*$ be a finite word. A (prefix-)suffix duplication step applied to $w$ produces a new word $w \cdot u$, where $u$ is either a prefix or a suffix of $w$. Starting from a single letter $a \in \Sigma$ and iterating such duplication steps, one obtains finite words; an infinite word $\mathbf{w} \in \Sigma^{\omega}$ is said to be generated by iterated (prefix-)suffix duplication if it is the limit of an infinite chain of finite words obtained by repeatedly applying these steps.

For a real number $\alpha > 1$, an infinite word $\mathbf{w}$ avoids $\alpha$-powers (or $\alpha^+$-powers) if no factor of $\mathbf{w}$ is a repetition of exponent $\geq \alpha$ (resp. $> \alpha$), where the exponent of a nonempty word $u$ is $|u|/p$ with $p$ the smallest period of $u$.

Determine the infimum
$$\alpha^* = \inf\{\alpha : \text{there exists a finite alphabet } \Sigma \text{ and an infinite word } \mathbf{w} \in \Sigma^{\omega} \text{ obtained by iterated (prefix-)suffix duplication that avoids } \alpha\text{-powers}\}.$$

In other words, what is the smallest exponent of repetition that can be avoided by some infinite word constructed by iterated (prefix-)suffix duplication?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches show related work on prefix-suffix duplication and prefix-suffix square completion, where it is known that infinite words generated by such operations can avoid repetitions of exponent greater than 2, but no source clearly establishes the minimum (infimum) exponent attainable specifically for iterated (prefix-)suffix duplication. The status appears to remain open or at least not definitively settled in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Prefix–suffix duplication
status_evidence.snippet: Studies infinite words generated by iterated prefix-suffix duplication operations.
status_evidence.claim: Discusses iterated prefix-suffix duplication but does not appear to settle the minimum avoidable repetition exponent.

status_evidence.title: Prefix-Suffix Square Completion
status_evidence.snippet: Infinite words generated by square completion can avoid repetitions of exponent greater than 2.
status_evidence.claim: Related operation results indicate exponent-2 avoidance is possible for a related model, but not directly the minimum exponent for prefix-suffix duplication.
